title: Tariff Threats, Macroeconomic Expectations, and Policy Communication Strategies: Experiments Based on a Multi-Agent System
abstract: arXiv:2608.30522v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Tariff threats can move household beliefs before policy is enacted, yet their rapidly changing language is difficult to study with conventional surveys. We build a multi-agent system that turns 300 households from the Michigan Surveys of Consumers into persistent large-language-model agents exposed to social-media information over several simulated months. Calibrated agents reproduce some distributional and demographic patterns in human survey data collected after the announcement of Liberation Day tariffs. Simulated experiments indicate that immediacy, rate salience, semantic progression, message complexity, narrative, and sender identity jointly shape inflation and unemployment expectations and their dispersion. Open-ended responses trace these effects to attention, ambiguity, credibility, and causal narratives. translated_title: 关税威胁、宏观经济预期与政策沟通策略：基于多智能体系统的实验
translated_abstract: 关税威胁可以在政策正式实施之前影响家庭信念，但其快速变化的语言难以用传统调查方法进行研究。我们构建了一个多智能体系统，将密歇根消费者调查中的300个家庭转化为持续运行的大语言模型智能体，并在数个模拟月份中让其接触社交媒体信息。经过校准的智能体能够复现“解放日”关税宣布后收集的人类调查数据中的部分分布特征和人口统计模式。模拟实验表明，即时性、利率显著性、语义演进、信息复杂度、叙事方式以及发送者身份共同塑造了通胀与失业预期及其离散程度。开放式回答将这些效应归因于注意力、模糊性、可信度和因果叙事。第二项实验发现，中央银行的解释说明能够协调信念，尽管其对平均预期的影响……
tldr: 该论文构建了一个基于大语言模型的多智能体系统，将密歇根消费者调查中的300个家庭转化为模拟智能体，发现关税威胁信息的即时性、复杂度、叙事和发送者身份等特征共同塑造家庭的通胀与失业预期，且央行沟通能够协调市场信念。
en_tdlr: This paper builds a multi-agent LLM system simulating 300 households from the Michigan Surveys of Consumers, showing that features of tariff threat messaging—such as immediacy, complexity, narrative, and sender identity—jointly shape households' inflation and unemployment expectations, and that central-bank communication can coordinate beliefs.
